threads.text: Whether formal discovery boundaries will damage the informal trust Northline earned through early support.

introduced.speaker: user
introduced.quote: If I suddenly arrive with a formal evaluation boundary, it could feel like we have become bureaucratic just when they need us.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: You do not need to present a governance ceremony.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: The two risks you named remain real: restricting prototypes may make discovery artificial, while careful language may still feel like distance to Northline.

responses.speaker: assistant
responses.quote: Neither step guarantees trust or a good product decision, but both make misunderstanding easier to notice before momentum chooses for you.

constraints.text: Reliability work has already been postponed twice.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Meanwhile we have reliability work we have postponed twice, and we told smaller customers that the next release would simplify the core workflow.

constraints.text: Smaller customers were promised a simpler core workflow in the next release.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Meanwhile we have reliability work we have postponed twice, and we told smaller customers that the next release would simplify the core workflow.

constraints.text: Lina believes roughly seventy percent of the reporting work could be reusable.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Also, Lina, our strongest engineer, thinks about seventy percent of the underlying work could become a general reporting layer.

constraints.text: Sales has already signaled serious consideration of a summer path without calling it a promise.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: The phrase “quiet commitment” is exactly what worries me, because our sales lead has already told them we are “looking seriously at a summer path.” He says that is not a promise. Northline probably hears more than that. I also do not know how to run discovery without signaling that the feature is coming. If we spend two weeks in their workflow, then say no, we might damage more trust than if we decline now.

constraints.text: Lina is one of two people carrying on-call and was hit hard by the last incident.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Lina is excited, but she is also one of two people carrying on-call, and the last incident hit her hard.

constraints.text: Northline can continue its manual CSV process for another quarter.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: They can live with their manual CSV process for another quarter, although their operations lead may move to a different role by then.

constraints.text: Northline's operations lead may move to a different role within that quarter.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: They can live with their manual CSV process for another quarter, although their operations lead may move to a different role by then.

constraints.text: Smaller customers currently want fewer confusing states and faster support, not reporting.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Northline emailed this morning. They can live with their manual CSV process for another quarter, although their operations lead may move to a different role by then. That reduces the urgency, but it also means we could lose the person who understands the problem best. Our smaller customers are not asking for reporting. They are asking for fewer confusing states and faster support. I am less sure this is a broad product signal than I was yesterday, but more sure the discovery could be valuable.
